story_description: As a user, I want to see visual badges on sidebar items indicating unread events so that I can quickly identify sessions with new activity without switching context.
task_description: Implement subtle pulse and fade animations for unread badge indicators that draw attention to new events while respecting system accessibility preferences for reduced motion.
atom_description: Add CSS-style pulse animation to unread badges when count increases, with automatic detection and respect for macOS accessibilityReduceMotion system preference.
problem_statement: When new events arrive in background sessions, users need visual attention cues to notice the badge count change. Static badges are easy to miss, especially in peripheral vision. Animation provides a non-intrusive way to draw attention, but must be disabled for users with motion sensitivity preferences.
scope_in: Implement subtle pulse animation on badge when unread count increases
Implement fade-in animation for badge appearance when count goes from 0 to 1
Detect and respect macOS accessibilityReduceMotion system preference
Use SwiftUI animation modifiers with appropriate duration and easing
Animation triggers only on count increase, not on count decrease or reset
scope_out: Badge count calculation logic (handled by T001-A001)
Badge styling and theming (handled by T002-A001)
Animation preferences beyond system reduce motion setting
assumptions: UnreadBadgeView component exists from T002-A001 and accepts animation parameters
Session unread count is observable via SessionStore published property
SwiftUI animation system supports conditional animation based on state changes
constraints: Animation duration must not exceed 300ms to avoid distraction
Must use declarative SwiftUI animations, not imperative CAAnimation
Must query reduce motion preference synchronously without async calls
Animation must complete fully or not start, no partial animations on view disappear
Must not cause layout shifts or badge position changes during animation
functional_requirements: FR1: Badge pulses with scale animation (1.0 to 1.15 to 1.0) when unread count increases
FR2: Badge fades in with opacity animation (0.0 to 1.0) when transitioning from 0 to non-zero count
FR3: Animation is completely disabled when accessibilityReduceMotion is enabled
FR4: Animation triggers only on count increase, not on decrease or manual reset
FR5: Multiple rapid count increases coalesce into single animation cycle
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Animation completes within 300ms total duration
NFR2: Animation uses easeOut timing curve for natural deceleration feel
NFR3: Animation does not impact scroll performance in sidebar list
NFR4: Zero CPU usage when animation is not active
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create BadgeAnimationModifier ViewModifier that encapsulates pulse and fade animations
Step 2: Add @State property to track previous unread count for change detection
Step 3: Implement onChange handler to detect count increases and trigger animation
Step 4: Query NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion at animation trigger time
Step 5: Apply scaleEffect and opacity modifiers with withAnimation block
Step 6: Add animation completion callback to reset animation state
Step 8: Test animation behavior with Accessibility Inspector reduce motion toggle
data_model_changes: N/A - Animation is purely presentational with no data model impact
event_contracts: N/A - Animation does not emit events, only responds to count changes
ui_states: Idle state: Badge displayed at normal scale (1.0) and full opacity (1.0)
Pulse animating state: Badge scales from 1.0 to 1.15 over 150ms then back to 1.0 over 150ms
Fade-in animating state: Badge opacity transitions from 0.0 to 1.0 over 200ms
Reduce motion state: All animations disabled, immediate state changes only
ui_interactions: System receives new event in background session, badge count increases, pulse animation triggers
User enables Reduce Motion in System Preferences, animation stops immediately
User switches to session, count resets to 0, no animation on decrease
Multiple events arrive rapidly, single coalesced pulse animation plays
ui_copy: N/A - Badge animation has no text copy
edge_cases: Count increases by more than 1 in single update: single pulse animation, not multiple
Count increases while animation already playing: queue next animation after current completes
View disappears mid-animation: animation completes in background without crash
Reduce motion toggled mid-animation: current animation completes, future animations disabled
Badge removed from view hierarchy during animation: no crash or leak
failure_modes: Animation fails to trigger: Badge still displays correct count, user sees static badge (graceful degradation)
Reduce motion check fails: Default to showing animation (safer than hiding important feedback)
Animation duration exceeds 300ms: Use transaction timeout to force completion
rollback_plan: Remove BadgeAnimationModifier import and usage from UnreadBadgeView.swift, delete BadgeAnimationModifier.swift file, badge reverts to static display without animation.

Visual verification: No animation plays when Reduce Motion enabled in System Preferences
perf: Verify animation does not cause dropped frames during sidebar scroll
Verify zero CPU usage when badge is idle with no count changes

security: N/A - Animation modifier has no security surface

acceptance_tests: Given a session with 0 unread events, when 1 event arrives, then badge fades in with opacity animation
Given a session with 3 unread events, when 2 more events arrive, then badge pulses once with scale animation
Given Reduce Motion is enabled in System Preferences, when events arrive, then badge updates without any animation
Given animation is in progress, when additional events arrive, then only one animation cycle plays
acceptance_criteria: Pulse animation scales badge to 1.15x and back within 300ms total duration
Fade-in animation transitions opacity from 0 to 1 within 200ms
Animation is completely disabled when accessibilityReduceMotion is enabled
No animation triggers on count decrease or reset to zero
All unit tests pass with animation timing verified

open_questions: Should animation trigger on app becoming active if count changed while in background?
Should there be a user preference to disable animation independent of system reduce motion?
notes: Animation is intentionally subtle to avoid being annoying. Pulse scale of 1.15x was chosen based on Apple HIG recommendations for attention-drawing without alarm. Duration of 300ms matches system alert animations.

na_justifications.event_contracts[0]: Animation does not emit domain events, only responds to count state changes

verification_steps: Run swift test --filter BadgeAnimationTests and verify all tests pass with green status
Toggle Reduce Motion in System Preferences > Accessibility > Display, launch app, trigger event, verify no animation plays
Trigger event in background session, observe badge pulse animation completes within 300ms

risks: Animation may cause motion sickness for sensitive users if reduce motion check fails
Animation timing may vary on older Macs causing visual jank
Rapid count updates may cause animation queue overflow
mitigations: Test reduce motion check on app startup and cache result
Use SwiftUI declarative animations which handle timing consistently across hardware
Implement coalescing to limit animation frequency to once per 300ms minimum
risk_register.blast_radius: Limited to UnreadBadgeView component in sidebar; animation failure results in static badge display which is acceptable fallback
risk_register.fallback_plan: If animation causes issues, set reduceMotion parameter to always-true to disable animation while keeping modifier in place, allowing easy re-enablement later
